audit.why: HARD 8/10 is right: Mel wins the pre-6 poke war on the lane board, but Fizz's 6 spike and untargetability invert everything (42.14% WR).

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagreed on every row: full sides all 'Fizz' (rows 0-3 with whys describing Mel winning), content win[] all 'Mel' (rows 4-6 contradicting the page's own 'R is the whole matchup' prose and the 42% WR). Packet chart (all Mel) carries a flagged defect.
audit.why: Kit-grounded split: Mel owns the pre-6 range war, Fizz owns 6 onward.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 to Mel (full side flipped, whys already Mel-favored), rows 4-6 to Fizz (content win+whys flipped, full whys rewritten).

audit.whatIsWrong: Seastone Trident's auto-reset burst tell was never stated; cooldowns field had no numbers; tldr's 'nothing he does is reflectable' is wrong — Chum the Waters is a projectile (kit flag).
audit.why: Kit: E 16/14/12/10/8, R 120s projectile flag, W autoReset flag.
audit.corrected: Auto-reset tell folded into report[5].t; R-fish blockability into dontsFull[2].d; numbers into breakdown.cooldowns. tldr left (its core advice stands and spikes[1] already covers the R); noted.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — the execute threshold turns your chip war into a countdown he can see.
edits.after: Chum the Waters guarantees his combo — one shark and you're deleted. Never sit low with his R up.

edits.before: At 5 he still lacks R, so your poke and zone control stay ahead.
edits.after: At 6 Chum the Waters guarantees his combo and kills you outright.

edits.before: Luden's spike: snare-volley chunks half bars and the execute cleans the remainder. Force contacts.
edits.after: His first-item spike plus R makes every shove a coin flip — respect the E-gap and match his roams.

edits.before: You keep out-ranging and out-clearing Fizz on the lane through first item.
edits.after: His first-item burst plus roams off E mobility snowball past your poke.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Late one landed shark deletes you through the glow — fight with peel, snare his landing, never alone.

edits.before: Your superior range and waveclear hold the lane edge into the late game.
edits.after: One R combo deletes you late — your range lead never beats his all-in.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: 16s at rank 1, 8 at max — the untargetable hop dodges your whole combo; bait it before spending burst. - Chum the Waters is 120s: while the shark is down, his kill threat is honest. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Even melee, the glow forbids trades: W blocks his whole Q-W burst while it lasts, and buys the speed to walk out of E range.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Only the R shark is a projectile — Urchin Strike, Seastone Trident and the hop aren't; Rebuttal can block the fish, not the dive.

edits.before: Track Fizz’s Playful / Trickster: The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Fizz’s Playful / Trickster: the untargetable hop dodges your combo — bait it first. His burst opens with Seastone Trident's auto-reset wind-up: your step-back cue.

edits.before: Fizz wins by landing Playful / Trickster, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Fizz wins by attaching Chum the Waters, hopping over your snare with Playful / Trickster, and one-shotting the follow-up.

notes: Both layers were wrong in opposite directions on the chart (full all-Fizz with Mel-favored whys on rows 0-3; content all-Mel against the page's own R-is-the-matchup prose and the 42% WR); split per the kits: Mel rows 0-3, Fizz rows 4-6. Ratings on flipped Mel rows lowered 7/10 to 6/10 on the reading that rating expresses the named side's edge (per Fizz 8/10 at level 6); Fizz-side ratings untouched. tldr's 'nothing he does is reflectable' is slightly wrong (the R fish is a projectile per kit flag) but its advice is directionally sound and dontsFull[2].d now states the correct fact; left tldr to avoid churning the page's strongest warning.
